title: Discord Rewrites Desktop and Mobile Clients in Rust Using Zed's GPU-Accelerated Rendering Framework
gist: Discord is rewriting its desktop and mobile clients in Rust (project Phoenix), dropping Electron for Zed's GPU-accelerated GPUI framework on desktop and React Native for native views plus a shared Rust core on mobile. Early builds show ~290 MB RAM and near-instant cold start versus 5.5 s on Electron, at the cost of rebuilding browser-provided features like text layout and accessibility.

themes.theme: Discord's exit from Electron and React Native

insights.claim: Discord is rewriting its desktop and mobile clients in Rust under project Phoenix, removing Electron and React Native, with mobile using native iOS/Android views and sharing app code with desktop via a common Rust core.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: A marquee consumer app abandoning Electron and React Native is a notable signal against cross-platform web-tech frameworks for performance-critical apps.
insights.quote: That means Electron goes away, and so does React Native, mobile keeps native UI but shares app code with desktop via Rust.
insights.locator: Vishnevskiy expanded on the rewrite on X

insights.claim: Discord chose GPUI, the GPU-accelerated Rust UI framework built by the Zed team, rather than Tauri for its desktop client.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Raises the profile of Zed's GPUI as a general-purpose app framework beyond the Zed editor; a potential ecosystem win for Zed.
insights.quote: And it’s not Tauri, it’s GPUI, so good guess everyone.
insights.locator: Vishnevskiy expanded on the rewrite on X

insights.claim: Discord has used Rust since 2018 for much of its infrastructure, voice tech and parts of the client, making a full Rust client the culmination of a long-running migration.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Shows Rust adoption progressing from backend infrastructure into client apps at large consumer companies.
insights.locator: Vishnevskiy expanded on the rewrite on X

insights.claim: Discord's browser client will keep rendering HTML with application logic compiled to WebAssembly, while embedded web surfaces like YouTube videos and Activities will use an OS webview.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Shared Rust core compiled to WebAssembly illustrates a single-codebase strategy across web, desktop and mobile.
insights.locator: The browser client keeps rendering HTML

insights.claim: Early internal Discord desktop builds use around 290 MB of RAM with two accounts logged in and cold-start near-instantly, versus a 5.5 second cold start on Electron.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Quantifies the performance penalty of Electron apps, strengthening the case for native/GPU-rendered alternatives.
insights.locator: Early internal builds for the desktop app

insights.claim: Discord's rewritten mobile app loads in under 2 seconds versus approximately 5 seconds for the legacy React Native app.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Evidence that native views outperform React Native in a large production app.
insights.locator: Vishnevskiy showcased similar improvements on mobile

insights.claim: A 2026 KTH master's thesis by Elias Floreteng found Swift beats React Native on every comparable runtime metric on iOS, while on Android the gap to native is small and runs both ways, with native ahead on memory and CPU.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: React Native's new architecture still trails native on iOS, which may weigh on its use for performance-sensitive apps.
insights.locator: Elias Floreteng, in his master’s thesis at KTH

themes.theme: Framework trade-offs: GPUI vs Tauri vs Electron

insights.claim: Tauri avoids bundling Chromium and yields smaller executables, but its RAM usage on Windows tends to match Electron because it still relies on resource-hungry browser technology via the OS webview, which can also behave inconsistently across operating systems.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Tauri's memory advantage over Electron is limited on Windows, weakening it as the default Electron replacement.
insights.locator: While Tauri also uses a Rust backend

insights.claim: GPUI replaces the browser engine with a hybrid immediate/retained-mode GPU-accelerated UI targeting 120 fps without garbage-collection pauses, but developers give up browser-provided text layout, input method integration, screen-reader accessibility and right-to-left support.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Accessibility and internationalization gaps are an execution risk for apps adopting GPUI and an opportunity for Rust UI library builders.

insights.claim: Zed is an open-source Rust code editor built by a team including the creators of GitHub's Atom editor, positioning itself on performance against VS Code.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Performance-focused developer tools are challenging VS Code's 'good enough for everyone' dominance.
insights.quote: VS Code won by being good enough for everyone. Zed wins by being excellent for developers who refuse to compromise on speed.
insights.locator: The desktop app thus drops Chromium/Node.js for GPUI
